Artificial Intelligence could spell the end of the human race

You know, it's kind of funny that I keep harping on Artificial Intelligence, when most of you have only a very dim idea that it's something to with computers, and it should be worried about at some point, but now now for heaven's sake. Sigh. Anyway, this article is surprisingly good, and really lays it all out there in black and white -- although sadly, most of you are going to skip it. Like I said often, it's by far the most important thing in the world -- everything else is really trivial, when you come right down to it. Ah well, I tried.

Why?

I feel we are projecting our own violence, hate, bigotry, onto the AI before it even exists.

I would argue an AI that would want to destroy humanity isn't an AI at all. A true intelligence, one that is supposedly "better" than us, would not want to destroy us at all, perhaps stop a lot of the things we do, perhaps change our way of life, but never destroy us. A sufficiently advanced AI would take an interest in life and human life particularly.

The saddest being in the universe is the AI left behind, millions of years in the future, alone, talking to itself.

FF7: Best Game Music of All Time?

I absolutely love most of the music composed by Nobuo Uematsu. I'm not exactly crazy about FFVII, but won't deny that the music is great - it's consistently good through the whole series. I went to see Distant Worlds last year and Final Symphony the year before that and it's all just so good.

I don't necessarily think it has the best music of all time, although it does have great music. I really like the music from FF8, FF9 and FF10 as well. You can't really count out nintendo as well! They have a lot of great music from something like the Legend of Zelda franchise.
There's pretty much never been a FF game with bad music. FF10 comes closest in my mind to the music in FF7
Even the SNES days with the 16 bit music was great. Many memorable tunes from the FF1-6 era.

I'd be with you if the title was: "Uematsu: best game composer of all time?" But he has scores better than FF7. Chrono Trigger, FF9, FF10, etc.

I'm also a huge fan of Glenn Stafford. He's basically the soundtrack of my childhood, and the one person I'd be willing to ask for an autograph from.

Goddamnit, how is everyone who worked on StarCraft a genius?

And I'm with you on Chrono Trigger and almost on FF10, but 9? I don't know. I mean, what's even one song from that game that comes close to matching the FF7 songs in the article?

i fully admit that it could be nostalgia talking, been way too long since i've listened to that stuff. maybe Loss of Me/Protecting My Devotion? Iifa tree comes to mind. Cleyra settlement is pretty good too. Cid's theme, but i don't remember what that sounds like, i only recall the name

this isn't compared to stuff in the article, btw; i didn't even read it
Final Fantasy music is amazing. I also love EVE Online soundtrack and from recent years Skyrim. All masterpieces for me.

Personally, I really enjoyed the soundtrack to The Last Story, also composed by Nobuo Uematsu.

I feel it doesn't come up often because it existed as a limited release on the Wii. It's unfortunate, because I think it's some of his best work.

The FF series has unbelievable music, and Uematsu is unquestionably a genius, but my vote still goes to SOTN.

https://m.youtube.com/watch?list=PL55DF16132A28F682&v=EjVoUFrdYFQ

Akira Yamaoka, on the first two Silent Hill games, was pretty great. It's not really stuff you can just listen to anytime like Uematsu or Soule and feel nostalgic. It was the kind of sound that helped place you into that world, more so than most soundtracks can.

I wouldn't say best of all time. Very iconic, but not greatest. I have liked other games music more, but that's just me opinion haha

I think Shining Force had some really great music too
